w:r.w:t: This note exists to be rendered. Every construct below is here because some renderer somewhere got it wrong. The prose is justified, sits at 1.15 line spacing, and runs long enough to wrap at least twice so that the line breaking itself can be compared between two builds of the same document.
A second paragraph, so the spacing between paragraphs is measurable. It carries
a highlighted span that a human still has to fill in
sitting inside the sentence rather than on a line of its own.
Punctuation matters too: “double quotes”, ‘single quotes’, an em dash — like this, an en dash – like that, and an ellipsis… all of which a smart-quotes pass rewrites.
A first bullet, long enough to wrap so that the hanging indent under it can be compared. The second line must line up under the first character of the text, not under the glyph.
A nested bullet, which should carry a hollow circle rather than a disc.
A third level, which should carry a filled square.
The second numbered item, long enough to wrap and check the hanging indent the same way the bulleted list does.
A nested number, which should be a lower-case letter.
A paragraph between the two lists, so the second list has to restart at one rather than carry on from three.
1.3.1-A narrow table with a date column
The date column must not break inside a date. A column narrower than its longest unbreakable token makes Word hyphenate the token itself.
Access to the production environment is granted only through the identity provider, and every grant carries an expiry. A quarterly review removes anything that outlived its purpose.
Shared accounts are prohibited. Where a system cannot support per-person credentials, the exception is recorded and reviewed at each renewal.
Break-glass credentials are sealed, and opening one raises an alert to the on-call engineer within one minute.
1.3.3-A table carrying marks and a link

A block quote, which this renderer flattens into ordinary prose rather than indenting. That is a deliberate choice in the reference implementation, and it has to be reproduced rather than improved on.
Text under the fourth level, which must be the same size as this prose and lighter in weight than the heading above it.
The author’s number wins, and the next computed heading follows on from it.
Appendix A: things that are never numbered
An appendix names itself, so it takes no computed number.
